get_sheet.description: A sheet's structure and state. Read it before choosing what to run or fix, then read_rows or a run tool. Answers the columns in order, row_count, data_version, row_generation, its description and limits (rows and columns left: check before a big append or import). column_details says for each column its kind (plain, ai, http, enrichment, waterfall, webhook, clean, formula, lookup), what fills it (fill: its newest run or its setup; filled_by names the column whose run fills it), the columns it reads, auto_run, run_if (the "Only run if" rule) and description. Prompts, formulas and URLs are cut short unless the column is named in columns; credentials in a URL read "…". include_counts adds filled, errors (a failed run or ❌) and empty (the rest: not run, skipped, running) per column, reading every row (up to 20 columns: those in columns, else the first). Also: filling_columns (their cells read "⏳ Processing..." until done), the setups of clean, formula and lookup columns (a lookup's broken says why it stopped, and kept_changing why rows it looked up may hold older values), active_runs and active_setup_runs (control_run cancel_all stops them all), views (pass view to read_rows or export_csv) and auto_dedupe (set_auto_dedupe's setting, or null).

read_rows.description: Read a sheet's rows as {id, index, data}, in index order, up to 100 a call. Pass columns: reading every column of a wide sheet is what makes reads expensive. Row ids stay the same across sorts: use them with update_cells and delete_rows. PAGES: cursor = the last row's index; next_cursor is null at the end. Paging a filtered read (where) echoes expected_data_version and expected_row_generation from the page before; a sheet that changed answers "restart paging". where filters by text, numbers, dates, lists of values, OR groups and run state ([{"operator":"has_error"}]). return_mode count or ids answers without cells. include_status reads run cells as {status, value, error}. group_by and aggregates count, sum and average per value without reading rows. row_ids (1 to 1000) returns those rows in that order with updated_at, and missing (list_trash has deleted ones); past about 40,000 characters read unread_ids next. Prefer it to re-read rows a run just touched. It takes only columns, include_status and max_chars_per_cell. updated_since returns rows changed at or after that UTC second, oldest first; page with cursor = next_cursor (text). To keep a copy up to date: when next_cursor is null, pass as_of as the next updated_since and dedupe by id; deleted rows don't show. It takes only columns, include_status, limit and cursor. max_chars_per_cell cuts long cells and lists them in cut_cells; read those whole with row_ids.

fields.columns: Only these columns. Omit for all (expensive on wide sheets). An item can also take one value out of a JSON cell (an HTTP API answer, say): {"column":"Response","path":["data","emails",0],"as":"Email"}. path is plain keys (an object's key, or a list position from 0), at most 5, not JSONPath; the value comes back as it is in the JSON (text, number, object, list), or null when the cell isn't JSON or has no such key. Without as, it is named "Response.data.emails.0".
fields.where: Rows must pass every item. An item is a condition {column, operator, value} or a group: {"or":[items]} passes when any of its items does, {"and":[items]} when all do, and a group's items can be groups, up to 5 deep. "enabled": false turns a condition off (kept, not counted). Text operators ignore case and outer spaces: eq, neq, contains, not_contains, starts_with, ends_with, empty and not_empty (no value); any_of and not_any_of take "values":["a","b"]. gt, gte, lt and lte need a number in the cell ("1,000" counts, "1,5" doesn't); other cells never pass. date_eq, date_neq, date_gt (after), date_gte, date_lt (before) and date_lte compare calendar days and need a date in the cell and in value: 2024-01-31, 2024/01/31, 1/31/2024 (month first unless the first number is over 12), 31.1.2024 (day first), Jan 31, 2024 or 31 Jan 2024, a time after it ignored; other cells never pass, date_neq included. Run-state operators read the words AI, HTTP API and enrichment runs write into cells, so you never parse them: has_error (the run failed, ❌), has_result (a real value), not_run (never run), condition_not_met (kept out by its "Only run if" rule), running (⏳ waiting or running, ➕ adding rows), out_of_date (a result made from input cells that changed since; control_run mode out_of_date reruns them). They take no value, and column is optional: left out, a row passes when ANY run column matches ([{"operator":"has_error"}] = rows where any run failed). An output column of a run reads the run's state from its status column, so has_error on "Email" finds the rows whose enrichment failed. Text operators compare the cell as written, status words included. Example: [{"column":"Industry","operator":"any_of","values":["SaaS","Fintech"]},{"column":"Signed up","operator":"date_gte","value":"2024-01-01"},{"or":[{"column":"Email","operator":"empty"},{"and":[{"column":"Phone","operator":"empty"},{"column":"Country","operator":"eq","value":"US"}]}]}].
fields.include_status: true: each AI, HTTP API and enrichment column's cell comes back as {status, value, error} instead of its text. status is done (value holds the result), no_result (the run finished without a value; reason says why when Cubex wrote one, e.g. "Not found"), error (error holds what failed), out_of_date (a result, value or reason as above, made from input cells that changed since: a rerun with mode out_of_date refreshes it), condition_not_met, running or not_run. Other columns are unchanged. Default false.
fields.group_by: Count rows per value of up to 3 columns instead of reading rows: groups ignore case and outer spaces (like eq), an empty cell is the group "". Answers rows_matched, group_count, the largest groups as {group, count, values} (by count, up to 1,000) and truncated when there were more. Takes where and view; not cursor, limit, columns, return_mode or include_status. On a column with very many different values (emails, ids) it stops past 100,000 groups. While the sheet is busy (an import, a sort, a column filling) it answers busy: try again when that finishes.
fields.aggregates: Per group (or over all rows without group_by): count (rows; with a column, its non-empty cells), sum, avg, min, max of a column. Numbers are read like gt/lt ("1,000" counts; text that isn't a number is skipped; null when none). Each comes back in values under "sum(Revenue)", "count", ...
fields.view: A saved view of the sheet, by name or id (get_sheet lists views): its filters are added to `where`, and when it hides columns its visible columns are the columns unless you pass columns. "active" reads the view the app shows. Reads through a view answer view_version: with a cursor, echo it as expected_view_version (and, when the view filters, expected_data_version and expected_row_generation).
fields.max_chars_per_cell: Cut each cell's text to its first N characters, N from 1 to 200,000. cut_cells then lists the cells cut by row id, then column, with each one's full length: {"<row id>": {"Notes": 5120}}, a row only when a cell of it was cut ({} when none). Characters count as JavaScript counts them (an emoji is 2): a cut never leaves half of a surrogate pair, but an emoji built from several characters (a skin tone, a flag, a family) can lose its last parts. With include_status a run cell's value or error is cut, never its status. A value a columns path takes out of a JSON cell: an object or list is cut as its JSON text (it comes back as text), numbers and true/false never. Rows only: not with group_by, aggregates or return_mode ids or count.

append_rows.description: Add up to 1000 rows at the end of a sheet, each as {column: value}. For a file, use create_upload_link instead (the file never passes through your context); to copy rows from another sheet, transfer_rows. The columns must exist (add_column first). Returns the new rows' ids and indexes, in the order given. With auto-dedupe on (set_auto_dedupe), a row whose key the sheet already had says kept: false (it went to the trash) and auto_dedupe says what was not kept or replaced. When auto-run is on, auto_run lists the columns that will fill the new rows on their own: an enrichment spends treg credit (estimated_usd), an HTTP API column sends real requests (sends_requests). Tell the user. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the same key and arguments within 24 hours answer as the first call did, with replayed: true, and write nothing; the same key with other arguments is refused. A replay leaves out auto_run (the first call set the runs off).

update_cells.description: Set cells on rows by their stable ids (read_rows gives them), in one of two forms. ONE ROW: {"row_id": "…", "data": {"Status": "Done"}} (sheet_id optional; when given, the row must be in it); returns the full row. MANY ROWS, all or nothing: {"sheet_id": "…", "updates": [{"row_id": "…", "data": {"Status": "Done"}}]} (up to 1000); returns {updated}. Columns must already exist (add_column first). Values: string/number/boolean; null clears a cell. Columns a run is still filling are refused. To fill a column from each row, use formula_column or transform_column (free) rather than writing every cell. idempotency_key makes a retry safe: the same key and arguments within 24 hours answer as the first call did, with replayed: true, and write nothing; the same key with other arguments is refused.

delete_column.description: Delete a column: it goes to the trash with its cells, its place, its description and its own setup (what makes it an AI, HTTP API, enrichment, waterfall, formula, lookup or clean column), and the answer's trash says until when and how to restore it (restore_from_trash). What other columns, views and settings said about it is removed now and does not come back with it: its own auto-run, filters and hidden columns in views, webhook mappings, fields another run writes into it, lookups in other sheets reading it, auto-dedupe on it; the restore answer lists each one so you can set it up again. With Settings keeping deleted things 0 days it is deleted at once (trash_id null). A big column's cells take a while: past a few seconds the answer's trash says state "moving" (they go on in the background, and a restore waits until they are all in). Refused for run-owned columns, columns an active run reads, webhook marker columns, and the last remaining column.

run_ai_column.description: Fill a column by running an AI prompt on each row: one OpenRouter call per row, paid. Prefer the free tools when they can do it: clean_column, formula_column, transform_column, lookup_column. For one value from several sources use waterfall_column; for treg.to data, run_enrichment. Writes "<column_name> (Output)"; output_columns writes several typed columns from ONE call per row (never run a second AI pass to reformat a first). A new run with output_columns on existing columns is refused. The prompt names columns as /column_name: lowercase, each run of other characters as _ (an unknown one is refused with a suggestion). Model: model, else the sheet's default, else the account's (list_models). Returns run_id at once: poll get_run_status, then read_rows or get_run_results. After a target_row_ids test, finish with control_run rerun mode "empty". web_fetch reads pages only on the sites in the cells the prompt references (/domain or /website); web_search searches the web, and its fees are usually most of the cost (search_engine, max_searches_per_row). COST CEILING: max_cost_usd refuses to start when the estimate's high end plus one row's most is above it, or the model has no known price unless allow_unpriced is true. It is also the run's hard spend limit; spend_limit_usd sets one without the check (with both, the lower one). A row starts only while what the run spent, plus the most its rows out and that row can cost (at least 8,000 output tokens at the model's listed prices), stays within the limit; otherwise it waits, or pauses with pause_reason spend_limit and its rows not started stay ⏳ (control_run resume with a spend_limit_usd of at least get_run_status's resume_least_usd). A call cut off before it answered counts at its most for the rest of the run. Spend can pass the limit only with web search or fetch, on a model with no listed price, on a server restart with calls out, or when a call reset within 2 seconds (so tried again) was billed. If OpenRouter's model list can't be read, the run pauses (pause_reason provider_errors); resume to retry. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

fields.search_engine: Needs web_search. auto (default): the model's own search if it has one (billed by its provider, OpenAI about $0.01 a search), else Exa. native: the model's own. exa: $0.007 a search ($0.012-$0.015 deep). parallel: $0.005, or $0.001 in turbo or fast mode. perplexity: $0.005.
fields.search_mode: Needs search_engine exa or parallel. exa: instant, fast, auto (default) $0.007; deep-lite, deep $0.012; deep-reasoning $0.015. parallel: turbo (English and Japanese only), fast $0.001; basic (default), advanced $0.005.
fields.max_searches_per_row: Most searches a row (1-10; needs web_search). OpenAI, Google and xAI models' own search can't be capped: search_engine auto then uses Exa, native is refused.
fields.web_fetch: Let the model open web pages, per row only on the sites (a URL or bare domain) in the cells the prompt references. With output_columns, the "(Data)" column lists the pages it used.
fields.max_content_tokens: Cut each page web_fetch reads to about this many tokens (100-100000). With it or max_pages_per_row pages are read through Exa ($0.001 a page); an OpenRouter workspace that limits web fetch engines must allow Exa, or the run pauses.
fields.run_if: "Only run if": rows that fail this rule are not run, cost nothing, and show "⏭️ Condition not met" (a real value an earlier run wrote is kept). The rule language is check_run_condition's (its description says every check). Example: ({{Industry}} is "SaaS" OR {{Industry}} is "Fintech") AND {{Employees}} > 50. CHAINS: give each next column a rule on the previous one's result, e.g. {{Fit (Output)}} is "yes", once that run has finished; rows the previous rule kept out count as empty, so they stay out too. Check a rule with check_run_condition (free), or have write_run_condition write one from plain words. Reruns of the column repeat its rule; estimate_only counts only the rows that pass.
fields.save_only: Store this setup as the column's and run nothing: no rows, no cost. Answers saved: true and run_id, the setup's record: control_run rerun with it runs the column this way, as do auto-run and its next run. Cells, and which rows read out of date, stay as they are. A new column is made empty. Not with estimate_only or the arguments only a run takes. Default false. On an existing AI column it replaces the setup. Not with output_columns.
fields.estimate_only: Price it and start nothing (no AI calls, no columns): rows_to_process, estimated_cost_usd, per_row_usd {low, high}, web_fees_usd, web_search, in_flight (OpenRouter holds each running call's possible cost, also on your own provider key, so a high concurrency can be refused with 402 before the balance runs out: follow its warning), own_provider_key and assumptions. Default false
fields.preview_rows: Run the prompt for real on the first N rows (up to 20): each output with its sources, cost, paid_with and tokens, and a full-run projection. Nothing is created. On your own provider key cost_usd is only OpenRouter's fee: projected_total_usd adds the provider's bill. Later estimates of this prompt use what it measured.
fields.webhook_id: A run webhook (list_run_webhooks) to notify when this run finishes, with a signed POST. Delivery isn't guaranteed: keep polling get_run_status, the notice only saves polls.

run_http_enrichment.description: Call your own HTTP JSON API once per row and put fields of each answer into new columns. For treg.to data use run_enrichment. url, headers and body fill {{column_name}} per row (cell values escaped for where they go); a {{name}} that is no column or saved key is refused at start. Or pass curl, a whole cURL command: a key in it is never stored in the column; save_keys saves it as a saved key (needs the "secrets" scope, as does naming a saved key), or write {{key_name}} of a saved key in its place; a $VARIABLE in a key's spot uses the saved key with that name. Each response_mapping entry takes one JSONPath field into a column (the first match; an object or list as JSON text; filters are refused: map $ and read it with formula_column). JSON answers only; private and internal addresses are blocked; GET and HEAD answers are reused for 5 minutes. RETRIES: 429 and 503 (any method), another 5xx or no answer for GET, PUT and DELETE (POST with retry_post), following Retry-After up to 60 s; a 4xx never. Returns run_id at once: poll get_run_status, then read_rows or get_run_results. estimate_only checks the URL and {{names}} without sending anything.

fields.save_keys: With curl: true saves each key in the command as a saved key under a suggested name, or { "<where>": "<name>" } for every key (e.g. { "Authorization header": "openai" }) picks the names.
fields.run_if: "Only run if": rows that fail this rule are not run, cost nothing, and show "⏭️ Condition not met" (a real value an earlier run wrote is kept). The rule language is check_run_condition's (its description says every check). Example: ({{Industry}} is "SaaS" OR {{Industry}} is "Fintech") AND {{Employees}} > 50. CHAINS: give each next column a rule on the previous one's result, e.g. {{Fit (Output)}} is "yes", once that run has finished; rows the previous rule kept out count as empty, so they stay out too. Check a rule with check_run_condition (free), or have write_run_condition write one from plain words. Reruns of the column repeat its rule; estimate_only counts only the rows that pass.
fields.save_only: Store this setup as the column's and run nothing: no rows, no cost. Answers saved: true and run_id, the setup's record: control_run rerun with it runs the column this way, as do auto-run and its next run. Cells, and which rows read out of date, stay as they are. A new column is made empty. Not with estimate_only or the arguments only a run takes. Default false. The only way to change an existing HTTP API column's setup: save it, then rerun the column with control_run.
fields.webhook_id: A run webhook (list_run_webhooks) to notify when this run finishes, with a signed POST. Delivery isn't guaranteed: keep polling get_run_status, the notice only saves polls.

write_run_condition.description: Write an "Only run if" rule from plain words ("SaaS or fintech companies with more than 50 people"), using ONE small call to the sheet's default AI model (or model). The model sees the column names and a few values from the first rows, so the rule matches the sheet's real spelling. Returns the rule, the model used, what the call cost, and the same check as check_run_condition. Nothing runs: pass check.rule as run_if to a run. You can also write a rule yourself (see check_run_condition). A request that needs judgment no column holds ("is a good fit") is refused: run an AI column that answers it first, then write a rule on that column. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap this is refused.

get_run_status.description: One run's state: status (pending, running, paused, completed, failed, cancelled), row counts, error_message and cost_usd so far. Poll it with wait_seconds: it answers when the status changes or the time is up (with 10 waits of your account open, at once with waited: false). "completed" means every row was processed, not that it worked: check failed_rows, then get_run_results. list_runs finds a lost run_id. pause_reason says why a run paused itself, and pause_message what to do: token_cap, spend_limit (resume with a higher spend_limit_usd; an AI run's least is resume_least_usd), provider_errors, storage (free disk space first), stalled, web_engine (allow Exa on OpenRouter's Server Tools page); an enrichment's is in enrichment (daily_limit, balance, no_key, unreachable and others). control_run resumes or cancels. waiting: its rows wait for a column another run (held_by) holds; a paused holder keeps them waiting. AI runs add concurrency, rows_paid_with, searches, web_search and spend_limit_usd; enrichment runs daily_limit, enrichment, providers and list; waterfall runs waterfall. On your own provider key cost_usd is only OpenRouter's fee; provider_cost_usd is the provider's bill. condition_skipped_rows (run_if) are not in total_rows. Status cells are Cubex's own words, never data: "✅ Found", "⏭️ Not found", "⏭️ Budget ran out" (the per-row cap), other "⏭️ ..." (skipped) or "❌ ..." (failed) with the reason, "⏳ Processing...", "⏭️ Condition not met" (run_if kept the row out, no cost). Verified email: "✅ Valid", "✅ Catch-all", "✅ Risky"; a rejected row fills Email status, never Email. Row-adding jobs: "➕ ..." while adding, waiting for fields or room, or removing a rerun's earlier rows, "✅ N rows added", "✅ Already there", "✅ No rows to add", "❌ Rows not added: <reason>". An empty status cell means the row hasn't run (rows missing an input stay empty).

control_run.description: Pause, resume or cancel a run, rerun a finished one, or stop every run on a sheet. A cancel keeps the answers the run wrote; rows it hadn't reached get back what they held. RERUN starts a NEW run with the column's latest setup and COSTS MONEY AGAIN (one call per row); check get_run_results first to know how many rows you will pay for. AI, enrichment and waterfall reruns need row_ids or mode ("errored" is the usual retry, "empty" the rest after a test, "missing" empty, ⏭️ or ❌, "out_of_date" input cells changed since); HTTP defaults to all. An output_columns AI run reruns whole. An enrichment rerun buys rows from treg again (answers it still holds cost less or nothing). Poll the new run_id with get_run_status. Lower concurrency after error_class "concurrency" or a provider's 429. A resumed run's spend counts toward this token's spend cap. CANCEL_ALL with sheet_id stops every active run and setup run on the sheet but turns no auto-run off: a column whose auto-run batch it stopped pauses (auto_run_paused), and auto_run_on lists columns where new rows still start runs (set_auto_run paused true with no column pauses them all). Calls already sent finish and are billed. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

undo_run.description: Undo what a finished run wrote: each cell it filled gets back what it held before (its outputs, (Data), status, "Answered by" and step columns), and so does its rows' out_of_date state. Use it when a run wrote wrong answers; to fill rows again instead, control_run rerun. It SKIPS a cell changed since (by a person, an agent or a newer run); cells in rows or columns deleted since count as gone. Nothing runs again and nothing is refunded. A restored cell's stored answer is never reused, so running it again bills again. Clean, formula and lookup columns reading a restored cell work it out again (free); no auto-run starts. Rows a list enrichment added to another sheet stay (delete_rows removes them). A run still going can't be undone (control_run cancel first). Newest first: while a newer run that wrote one of its columns can be undone, an older one is refused. Each run once, for 7 days after it started. Pass run_type and run_id (list_runs, get_sheet's column_details), or sheet_id and column for that column's newest run. Returns state and how many cells were restored, skipped and gone; a big undo answers state undoing and goes on in the background (the sheet is busy meanwhile: call again with dry_run true to see how far it got).

get_run_results.description: Each row's outcome in a run: row id, status, error message and an error_class saying what to DO. Use it when cells are blank or wrong, instead of rerunning blind. AI classes: "retryable" (a rerun works), "prompt_content" (your wording: a rerun just bills again), "model_output" (try another model), "concurrency" (rerun with a lower concurrency), "configuration" (fix a setting), "unknown". HTTP classes: "retryable" (rate limit, timeout, 5xx), "not_found" (404 or 410; on every row, a wrong URL path), "configuration" (URL, auth, headers, {{name}}, JSONPath, blocked address), "response_format" (not JSON), "unknown". Retry only the transient ones with control_run rerun (mode errored for AI, missing for HTTP). Rows add cost_usd (an AI row on your own provider key: only OpenRouter's fee, and provider_cost_usd); AI rows paid_with, tokens and searches; enrichment rows found_by; waterfall rows answered_by and trace (each step reached: outcome, value, cost). include_answers adds each row's stored answer (up to 10 rows a page), to find paths for add_enrichment_field; on an HTTP run that used saved keys it needs the 'secrets' scope. Pages by cursor.

export_csv.description: Export sheet rows as CSV text. The CSV comes back IN YOUR CONTEXT, so a wide or long sheet is EXPENSIVE: always pass columns and where. Use it only when you need CSV itself (to hand on or save as it is); to reason over data, read_rows is cheaper and pages; for a file of any size, create_download_link. At most 40,000 characters come back: past that the answer says truncated: true and rest says how to get the others. Values are escaped against spreadsheet formula injection. Read-only.

fields.view: A saved view of the sheet, by name or id (get_sheet lists views): its filters are added to `where`, and when it hides columns its visible columns are the columns unless you pass columns. "active" reads the view the app shows. Reads through a view answer view_version: with a cursor, echo it as expected_view_version (and, when the view filters, expected_data_version and expected_row_generation).

manage_sheet.description: Create, rename, copy, delete or reorder the sheet tabs of a table (a table always keeps at least one sheet). create auto-names the sheet when name is omitted and can insert after a given tab. copy makes a new sheet right after sheet_id holding its values: the same rows in the same order under the same column names (or only the columns you list), as plain columns that nothing fills (no runs, formulas, lookups, rules or views come along), with a run's status words (⏳, ❌, ⏭️, ➕) left empty. Free, no AI; name defaults to "Copy of <sheet>". Use it to keep a sheet as it is now, for example before running its columns again; it answers once every row is in (rows_copied). delete puts the sheet in the trash whole (rows, columns, runs, views, webhook), cancels its active runs and stops its webhook; it is kept for the days set in Settings (30 by default; 0 deletes at once), and restore_from_trash brings it back. Enrichment results its columns bought that were not yet added as rows in another sheet are dropped (list_results_dropped says how many and for which sheets). Returns the table's updated tab list.

import_csv.description: Import CSV text into a sheet. The header row names the columns; new columns are created, and columns matching existing names (exactly) append into them. mode "append" adds rows after the existing ones; mode "replace" deletes all existing rows first (they go to the trash as one batch: restore_from_trash brings them back). Fails on columns an active run owns. Max ~2MB of CSV per call. For a file, use create_upload_link instead: any size, and the contents never pass through your context. When auto-run is on in the sheet, auto_run lists the columns that will fill the imported rows on their own (an enrichment spends treg credit, an HTTP API column sends real requests): tell the user. When cells look like text read with the wrong character set (they hold U+0080-U+009F, a sequence that lost one of those bytes, as "FraudFighterâ¢", or fix_encoding would change them, as with "CafÃ©"), the answer adds garbled_cells (how many) and garbled_samples (where the first 10 are, as {"<row id>": ["<column>", ...]}, without their values: read_rows with those row_ids shows them), and its note says clean_column with cleaner fix_encoding repairs them; their U+0080-U+009F characters are kept either way.

create_upload_link.description: Import a CSV file of any size (up to 500 MB) into a sheet without its contents passing through your context. Returns a one-time link; upload the file to it with the curl command in the result, from any machine that can reach Cubex. curl prints the import result (rows imported, new columns). When cells look like text read with the wrong character set (they hold U+0080-U+009F, a sequence that lost one of those bytes, as "FraudFighterâ¢", or fix_encoding would change them, as with "CafÃ©"), the answer adds garbled_cells (how many) and garbled_samples (where the first 10 are, as {"<row id>": ["<column>", ...]}, without their values: read_rows with those row_ids shows them), and its note says clean_column with cleaner fix_encoding repairs them; their U+0080-U+009F characters are kept either way. Same header rules as import_csv; mode "replace" deletes all existing rows when the file arrives (to the trash, restorable). The link works once and expires in 15 minutes. Needs the write scope. This token has no write permission, so this tool will refuse.

create_download_link.description: Save a sheet, or the columns and rows you pick (as in export_csv), as a CSV file of any size without its contents passing through your context. format jsonl saves JSON lines instead: one {"id", "data"} object a row, as read_rows answers it, with its values' types and no formula quote. Returns a one-time link; download it with the curl command in the result to save it anywhere on your machine, or give the link to the user to open in a browser. The link works once and expires in 15 minutes. Until then anyone who has it can download the data, so give it only to the user. The file holds the rows up to the last one the sheet had when the download begins. CSV values are escaped against spreadsheet formula injection.

fields.view: A saved view of the sheet, by name or id (get_sheet lists views): its filters are added to `where`, and when it hides columns its visible columns are the columns unless you pass columns. "active" reads the view the app shows. Reads through a view answer view_version: with a cursor, echo it as expected_view_version (and, when the view filters, expected_data_version and expected_row_generation).

run_enrichment.description: Run a treg.to enrichment once per row: work emails, phones, person or company data, or lists whose results become rows in another sheet. For several sources in one column use waterfall_column. Find the tool with search_enrichments, then read it with get_enrichment. COSTS MONEY: each row is a paid treg call on the user's treg balance (providers on the team's own keys bill the team). Call estimate_only:true first and tell the user the range; it creates nothing. A row whose exact lookup found something within the days set in Settings reuses it at $0. max_cost_per_row_usd caps each row and spend_limit_usd the run (it pauses there). The account's daily_limit caps ALL enrichments per UTC day (limit_usd null: off): a run that reaches it pauses; tell the user, who can raise it in Settings (a token can't). A row whose providers all answer 429 asks again for free (rate_limit_retries), then fails; lower concurrency if 429s go on. LIST JOBS (get_enrichment adds_rows:true) need list: run with test:true, wait for get_run_status to say completed, read the fields with get_list_fields, pick them with add_list_rows, then control_run rerun mode "empty"; or pass list.fields. destination_auto_run lists the auto-runs the new rows set off there, and chained_auto_run this sheet's auto-runs that read what the run writes (HTTP ones send real requests). Returns run_id at once: poll get_run_status (run_type "enrichment"). SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

fields.run_if: "Only run if": rows that fail this rule are not run, cost nothing, and show "⏭️ Condition not met" (a real value an earlier run wrote is kept). The rule language is check_run_condition's (its description says every check). Example: ({{Industry}} is "SaaS" OR {{Industry}} is "Fintech") AND {{Employees}} > 50. CHAINS: give each next column a rule on the previous one's result, e.g. {{Fit (Output)}} is "yes", once that run has finished; rows the previous rule kept out count as empty, so they stay out too. Check a rule with check_run_condition (free), or have write_run_condition write one from plain words. Reruns of the column repeat its rule; estimate_only counts only the rows that pass.
fields.save_only: Store this setup as the column's and run nothing: no rows, no cost. Answers saved: true and run_id, the setup's record: control_run rerun with it runs the column this way, as do auto-run and its next run. Cells, and which rows read out of date, stay as they are. A new column is made empty. Not with estimate_only or the arguments only a run takes. Default false. With add_to_column: true it replaces an existing column's setup. Not for a list job.

waterfall_column.description: Fill ONE value per row (a work email, phone, domain, LinkedIn URL or any text) by trying ordered steps and stopping at the first answer; for one source, run_enrichment or run_ai_column is simpler. Steps: enrichment (a treg.to tool from search_enrichments), ai (a prompt), http (your JSON API), formula (free JavaScript over {{input_key}}) or lookup (free: another sheet's return_column where match_column matches the input; put it first to skip paid steps). inputs maps each input key ONCE to a column or {"value": fixed}; steps read keys, never columns (treg tools take first_name, last_name, full_name, domain, company, linkedin_url, email). A value result_type can't read is no answer, and the next step runs. A row with none of a step's requires key sets skips it for free. check: verify (treg's email verify, paid) or a formula over {{value}}. column_name holds the answer, "⏭️ Not found" or "❌ <step>: <why>"; "<column> (Answered by)" names the step. COSTS MONEY: enrichment steps bill the treg balance, ai steps OpenRouter. estimate_only DEFAULTS TO TRUE: cost and answer rate per row and per step, nothing created: tell the user, then call again with estimate_only false. A treg answer found within the days set in Settings is reused at $0. spend_limit_usd caps the run. The account's daily_limit caps ALL enrichments per UTC day (limit_usd null: off): a run that reaches it pauses; tell the user, who can raise it in Settings (a token can't). add_to_column runs an existing waterfall column again, keeping its setup unless you pass new parts. dry_run writes nothing and returns each row's trace; a real run then reuses what it bought at $0 for 7 days. action "describe" (read scope) returns a column's setup in this shape to edit and send back (without the secrets scope HTTP keys read "…" and are kept when sent back with the same id and URL). Returns run_id: poll get_run_status (run_type waterfall), then get_run_results for the traces. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

fields.run_if: "Only run if": rows that fail this rule are not run, cost nothing, and show "⏭️ Condition not met" (a real value an earlier run wrote is kept). The rule language is check_run_condition's (its description says every check). Example: ({{Industry}} is "SaaS" OR {{Industry}} is "Fintech") AND {{Employees}} > 50. CHAINS: give each next column a rule on the previous one's result, e.g. {{Fit (Output)}} is "yes", once that run has finished; rows the previous rule kept out count as empty, so they stay out too. Check a rule with check_run_condition (free), or have write_run_condition write one from plain words. Reruns of the column repeat its rule; estimate_only counts only the rows that pass.
fields.save_only: Store this setup as the column's and run nothing: no rows, no cost. Answers saved: true and run_id, the setup's record: control_run rerun with it runs the column this way, as do auto-run and its next run. Cells, and which rows read out of date, stay as they are. A new column is made empty. Not with estimate_only or the arguments only a run takes. Default false. With add_to_column: true it replaces an existing column's setup.

set_auto_run.description: Turn auto-run on or off for an enrichment or HTTP API column, or pause and resume it. When on, the column repeats its newest run on new rows and on rows whose inputs get filled, once a row; rows already there are left alone. Clean and formula columns follow their source columns instead, free and without run_if or caps (turning a formula column on again lifts a pause). A resume takes waiting_rows for the rows that waited meanwhile. An enrichment's daily_cap_usd is never above the daily limit. An enrichment auto-run SPENDS the treg balance on every new row; with a webhook on the sheet, anyone with its URL can add rows that spend. An HTTP API auto-run SENDS REAL REQUESTS (leads to a sequencer, messages), once per row. The account's daily_limit caps ALL enrichments per UTC day (limit_usd null: off): a run that reaches it pauses; tell the user, who can raise it in Settings (a token can't). Returns every auto-run on the sheet. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

ai_visibility.description: Check whether AI engines recommend a brand, and track it over time. action "create" (free, asks nothing) makes a table "AI visibility for <brand>": a Questions sheet (per engine a column asking it, its answer, and "You in <engine>": "1st of 4" = your place among the brands named, or "Not named"; "Named by": how many engines name you; "Named first": the brand most engines name first) and a Cited sites sheet (every source an answer cites, with "Your site"). Brands are matched as whole words, ignoring case and accents, among brand and other_brands only. action "ask" (run scope) asks every engine the questions not asked yet: PAID treg calls, one enrichment run per engine (follow them with get_run_status, run type enrichment); the formula columns fill as answers come. action "check_again" (weeks later) copies Questions and Cited sites, values only, into sheets named with the day they were asked, adds "Named by on <date>" and "Change since <date>" ("Up 2", "Down 1", "Same", "New"), then asks every question again: also PAID, and it notes answers under three weeks old (a change then is mostly the usual variation). A stopped check is picked up by the next one. ask and check_again: estimate_only DEFAULTS TO TRUE and returns the cost; call again with estimate_only:false to start. action "set_brands" changes the brands and works every row out again (free). Read the table with read_rows (group_by Named first, or Domain on Cited sites, for counts). Answers vary between asks: compare totals, not one question.

get_balances.description: What the account can spend, read live: treg {balance_usd, on_hold_usd} for enrichments, enrichment_daily_limit {limit_usd, used_today_usd, remaining_usd}, and openrouter for AI runs {balance_usd (account credits, often null: OpenRouter shares it only with a management key), key_limit_usd, key_limit_remaining_usd, key_usage_usd, byok_usage_usd, available_usd, checked_at (when Cubex read them; a read is reused for 30 seconds)}: OpenRouter's numbers can lag behind runs that just finished, while access_token.spent_usd is live. A part that is not set up or can't be reached says so in error. Read-only: starts nothing and costs nothing. Use it before a large run, or when a run paused on balance. OpenRouter holds each running AI call's possible cost, so a high concurrency needs more free credit than the run will spend: run_ai_column's estimate_only reports that as in_flight. access_token {spend_cap_usd, spent_usd, left_usd} is this token's own spend cap on AI and enrichments (null: no cap), for its whole life, not per month.

get_usage.description: What AI, HTTP and enrichment runs cost and how much they ran, from the run records (never the rows), by column, day or run, for one sheet or the whole account. For what is left to spend use get_balances. Each row and the totals give runs, cells (rows run), reused_cells (filled at $0 from an earlier answer), ai_cost_usd (OpenRouter), provider_cost_usd (the user's own provider key), enrichment_cost_usd (treg), total_cost_usd and cost_per_cell_usd. Days are UTC and a run counts on the day it started. AI previews and AI helpers (write_formula, write_run_condition) count too, as kind preview or assist. Totals cover the whole range; rows_total says how many rows there are (GET /api/v1/usage with format=csv has every row). Deleted columns and sheets are included (column_deleted, sheet_deleted). Read-only: costs nothing.

get_version.description: Which Cubex version this server runs and whether a newer release is out: version (the running release, like "v0.8.12"; null for a build from a branch or a local source, or one that doesn't record its version, such as Docker), build (the build as the installer recorded it, null when not recorded), pinned_ref (an install made with --ref stays on that ref: `cubex update` reinstalls it, and getting newer releases needs the install command run again without --ref; null otherwise), update_check (the daily release check is on; the user turns it off in Settings), latest_release {version, published_at, notes_url, checked_at} (null when the check is off or has no answer yet) and update_available (null when it can't be told). Reads what the check kept: it never asks GitHub itself. On a newer release, an install made with the installer and not pinned updates with `cubex update`; others follow the release notes. With since (the version you last used), it adds changes_since {since, releases: [{version, changes: [{change: added, changed, removed, renamed or server, tools, replaced_by, summary, details}]}], note}: what changed for agents in every release after it, oldest first. Call it when a tool you expect is missing or the version is not the one you knew. Read-only: costs nothing.

list_trash.description: What was deleted and can still be restored: batches of rows (delete_rows, remove_duplicates, auto-dedupe, a CSV import that replaced rows, transfer_rows moving rows out, a list job's rerun, the app), whole sheets, whole tables and columns (delete_column). Each item has its trash_id, what it was, how and by whom it was deleted, and expires_at (kept for kept_days, set in Settings; then deleted). Without trash_id: the list, newest first (how auto_dedupe with a sheet_id lists what auto-dedupe removed there, one batch a day). With trash_id: that item, and for a batch or a column its rows (cells as they were, seq, row_id, old_row_index) a page at a time, or only rows holding a text (a search reads part of a big batch per call; next_after goes on). A column in state "moving" is still getting its cells: restore it once it reads "kept". Read-only. Next: restore_from_trash.

restore_from_trash.description: Put deleted things back from the trash (list_trash shows them). Costs nothing. trash_ids restores whole items (tables, then sheets, then columns and row batches, newest deletion first); trash_id with seqs restores only those rows of one batch (at most 1000). A sheet or table comes back whole (rows, columns, runs, views, webhook), renamed "<name> (restored)" if the name was taken. Rows go back to their old places when the sheet was not sorted, replaced or deduplicated since and those are free, else to the end in order; columns they need are added again (columns_added); a sheet without room refuses. Rows moved out with transfer_rows stay in their new sheet too. Auto-run does not run restored rows. A column comes back at its old place with its setup and auto-run off (renamed if its name was taken); its cells go only on rows that still exist and are empty there (cells_kept: rows holding a value now; cells_skipped: rows gone; both stay in the item). Rerun an AI or HTTP API column with control_run and setup.run_id; a clean, formula or lookup column works its rows out again. references_dropped lists what did not come back, each with redo (the tool to set it up again). A column whose request reads saved API keys needs the secrets scope. A refused item is in results with its error; the others still go. Refused while a run is active on the sheet. A big batch answers state "restoring" and finishes in the background.

clean_column.description: Clean a column into a new column for FREE: no AI, no credits, no requests, nothing leaves Cubex. Prefer it over run_ai_column for any cleanup it covers, and over transform_column and formula_column for names, companies, emails, phones and domains (the domain cleaner takes the root domain out of an email or a URL). The name and company cleaners drop emoji, read full-width characters as plain ones, and leave a placeholder cell (n/a, none, null, unknown, test, -) blank. Writes into column (default "<source_column> (clean)", or "(first name)", "(last name)", "(domain)"), always a new column: naming a clean column already there replaces its setup and cleans every row again; any other existing column is refused. Waits for the fill up to 10 seconds and returns cleaned_rows and blank_rows (values the cleaner could not read); a bigger sheet returns status "filling". Next: read_rows to check it.

fields.cleaner: person_name (fixes ALL CAPS or lowercase, keeping DeShawn and McDonald; turns "Smith, John" around; drops Mr/Dr/Jr/PhD and nicknames), first_name ("J. Michael Fox" gives "Michael"; never the last name), last_name (keeps "van", "de la"), company_name (drops Inc, LLC, GmbH and other legal endings, ", a company of X" and stray brackets; fixes ALL CAPS), email (lowercase; blank when the format is invalid, which says nothing about delivery), domain (the root domain of a website or email: "https://blog.acme.co.uk/x" gives "acme.co.uk"), phone (blank when not a real number), title_case (keeps small words and acronyms: "VP of Sales"), lowercase, trim (also inner spaces, line breaks and invisible characters), fix_encoding (repairs UTF-8 read as Windows-1252 or Latin-1: "CafÃ©" gives "Café"; what it can't repair stays as it was)

formula_column.description: To clean names, companies, emails or phones, or to take the domain out of an email or a URL, use clean_column instead. Fill a column for FREE with a formula worked out from each row: no AI, no credits, no requests. Prefer it over run_ai_column whenever the value can be computed from the row: picking a field out of an API response, choosing an item of a list by a condition, joining or splitting text, math. The formula is ONE JavaScript expression reading cells as {{Column name}}, e.g. {{Response}}?.emails?.find(e => e.type == "work")?.value or `${{{First}}} ${{{Last}}}` or Number({{Price}}) * 1.2. Cells are text: use Number() for math. A cell holding JSON (text starting with { or [, like a whole HTTP response written by run_http_enrichment mapping "$") arrives parsed, so find/filter/map work on it; this is how to pick an item by a condition, which JSONPath mappings refuse. Status cells ("⏳ Processing...", "❌ ...", "⏭️ ...") read as empty. Use optional chaining (?.) and return "" when data is missing. _ is Lodash. There is no network or file access. The result is written as text (objects and lists as JSON; null, undefined and NaN as an empty cell). A row the formula cannot work out shows "❌ <the error>" and counts in error_rows (first_error names the first). Writes into column, always a new column: naming a formula column already there replaces its formula and works every row out again, hand edits included; any other existing column is refused. Check a formula with preview:true first. write_formula writes one from plain words. Waits for the fill up to 10 seconds and returns filled_rows and error_rows; a bigger sheet returns status "filling".

write_formula.description: Write a formula for formula_column from plain words ("the work email from Response", "first and last name joined"), using ONE small call to the sheet's default AI model (or model). The model sees the column names and what the first rows hold (the shape of JSON cells), and the formula is checked on the first rows before it is returned. Returns the formula, the model used, what the call cost, and a preview (samples with their inputs and results). Nothing is saved: pass formula to formula_column. You can also write the formula yourself. A request that needs judgment or outside data is refused: use run_ai_column or an enrichment for that. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap this is refused.

lookup_column.description: Fill a column for FREE from ANOTHER sheet (any table): each row's source_column is matched against match_column of other_sheet_id, and the column gets the first match's value, Yes/No, a count or a list (returns). No AI, no credits. Use it to bring a company's data onto its people, check whether a row is already in another list, or count related rows, rather than reading both sheets into your context. Matching ignores case (accents too) and surrounding spaces; status cells (⏳, ❌, ⏭️) read as empty on both sides. A row it cannot answer honestly shows "❌ <why>" (a contains value under 3 characters, over 10,000 contains matches) and counts in error_rows. The other sheet is read as it is when each row is worked out: later changes there do NOT update the column (call again to look every row up again). Renaming columns there updates the lookup; deleting that sheet or a column it reads stops it (broken says why). Writes into column, always a new column (naming a lookup column already there changes it). Waits for the fill up to 10 seconds; a bigger sheet returns status "filling" (contains on very large sheets can take minutes). Refused while a run fills match_column or a column it returns. While a run or fill writes a column it reads, or that sheet is sorted, replaced or deduplicated, the fill waits ("waiting") and then looks every row up again, at most 3 times (then kept_changing names what kept changing: rows looked up before may hold older values; call again to redo them). Lookups that would wait for each other in a loop fail, naming each column. Returns filled_rows and error_rows. Next: read_rows to check it.

remove_duplicates.description: Find duplicate rows in a sheet and remove them, for FREE (no AI, no credits). Rows are duplicates when every listed column matches, ignoring upper/lower case and extra spaces. Each column can match as: text (default), email, domain ("https://www.acme.com/x", "jo@acme.com" and "acme.com" all match; a free email address such as Gmail never matches by domain, and a page on a shared site such as facebook.com/acme matches only the same page), phone (any format, an extension kept apart; phone_country, default US, says how bare digits are read), company (ignores Inc, LLC, Corp and other legal endings) or person_name ("Smith, John" matches "John Smith"; Jr and Sr kept apart). One row of each group stays: keep first (default, the highest row), last, or most_complete (fills the most cells; the highest of a tie). A row with any listed column empty, unreadable as its match, or holding a run status such as "⏭️ Not found" is never removed. Works on the whole sheet (filters do not apply). dry_run DEFAULTS TO TRUE: it changes nothing and returns how many rows would go, with sample groups (row ids and the key cells) and the largest group, so you can check what "duplicate" meant. Then call again with dry_run: false to remove. Removed rows go to the trash as one batch, kept for the days set in Settings (30 by default; 0 deletes at once): the answer gives its trash_id, and restore_from_trash puts them back. Their AI and HTTP results go. Refused while a run is active on the sheet. Prefer it over read_rows plus delete_rows.

set_auto_dedupe.description: Keep ONE row per key in a sheet as rows arrive, for FREE (no AI, no credits). Pick one key column and a match as in remove_duplicates. A row that arrives (webhook, append_rows, import_csv, transfer_rows, enrichment list rows) or whose key is typed in is checked against the rows there; on a match, keep oldest (default: the new row is not kept) or newest (it replaces the older ones, enriched cells included). Blank keys, run statuses and cells over 200 characters never match. Removed rows go to the trash (list_trash with how auto_dedupe, one batch a day; restore_from_trash puts them back unchecked). Rows already in the sheet stay: get_sheet's auto_dedupe.shared_rows counts those sharing a key, and remove_duplicates cleans them once. The key column must be one rows arrive with, not an AI, HTTP, enrichment, waterfall, clean, formula or lookup column; to match a cleaned value, pick the raw column with a match (a website column as domain). The answers of the tools that add or edit rows say which were not kept or were replaced. Call again to change it (fields left out stay). Refused while a run is active on the sheet.

save_setup.description: Save filled columns of a sheet as a named setup, to build the same columns on another sheet later. Name any column a step made (an AI column's "(Output)", an HTTP API or enrichment status column or one of its output columns, a clean or formula column). include_upstream (default true) adds every filled column they read, down the chain, so the setup holds the whole flow. Each step is saved as its column is set up now: prompt, model, web search, output columns, request, JSONPaths, enrichment choices, formula, cleaner, "Only run if" and auto-run. Saved keys are kept by name, never their value. A column that adds rows to another sheet can't be saved. preview: true returns what the setup would hold (its steps in order, inputs and keys) and saves nothing. Saving changes nothing in the sheet.

apply_setup.description: Build a saved setup's columns (list_setups) on a sheet and fill them, each step once the columns it reads are filled: a whole chain of columns on another sheet (for one column, use its own tool). COSTS MONEY: AI steps call your model per row, enrichments spend your treg balance, HTTP API steps send a request per row; clean and formula steps are free. ESTIMATE_ONLY DEFAULTS TO TRUE: the first call prices each step and starts nothing; tell the user, then call again with estimate_only:false. A step whose columns this setup made before CARRIES THEM ON, filling only rows it hasn't done: call again with the same inputs and names to fill new rows or finish a stopped run (get_setup_run shows the choices a run used). Auto-run is turned on only after a run on every row. Saved keys in its requests need the "secrets" scope. COST CEILING: max_cost_usd refuses to start (nothing is created) when the estimate's high end, plus one row's most for each AI step, is above it, or when a step has no known price unless allow_unpriced is true. Each started AI and enrichment step gets a spend limit within what is left of the ceiling (one with no known price runs without one). Returns a setup_run with each step's run_id (get_run_status works on those); follow it with get_setup_run. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). At the cap, new AI and enrichment runs, previews and AI helpers are refused, and running ones pause (resume them once the cap is raised; an auto-run goes on by itself). HTTP API runs cost nothing here and go on. Calls already in flight finish and count, so spend can pass the cap by those alone: an AI run's concurrency of rows (default 5, at most 100) in each of up to 4 runs, a preview's 20 rows (at most 3 previews), an AI helper's one or two small calls. An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

run_columns.description: Run several of a sheet's run columns (AI, HTTP API, enrichment, waterfall) again in one call, each with its own settings, on the rows mode picks, among row_ids or the rows a where matches. A column reading another chosen column (also through formula, clean or lookup columns) waits for that one's whole run. COSTS MONEY as each column's rerun does. ESTIMATE_ONLY DEFAULTS TO TRUE: the first call prices each column and starts nothing; tell the user, then call again with estimate_only:false. max_cost_usd refuses to start (nothing is created) when the estimate could pass it; once started, each AI, enrichment and waterfall column gets a spend limit from what is left. To change a column's setup use its own tool. Returns a setup_run: follow it with get_setup_run; control_setup_run pauses, resumes or stops it. SPEND CAP: this access token may spend $5.00 in all on AI and enrichments (for its whole life, not per month); $4.00 was left when this tool list was loaded (get_balances says what is left now). An enrichment or waterfall run holds room for its rows at their per-row cap, so it stops before the cap (with no per-row cap, once what was billed reaches it).

list_setup_versions.description: A setup version is a named copy of how a sheet's columns are set up, never their values: every column in order with its description, what fills it (an AI column's prompt, model and settings; an HTTP API, enrichment or waterfall column's request or choices; a clean, formula or lookup column's settings), its "Only run if" rule and auto-run. Without version_id: the sheet's versions, newest first (name, when, who saved it, how many columns and filled columns; auto true for a copy a restore kept of the setup it replaced). With version_id: that version against the sheet now, the same answer as restore_setup_version with dry_run: each column the version names that is gone (restoring adds it back, empty), set up differently (field by field, version vs now), filled another way now (restoring leaves it) or not in the version (it stays). Changes nothing. Request URLs are masked, headers show by name and request bodies only as changed.

restore_setup_version.description: Put a sheet's column setup back as a setup version (list_setup_versions) has it. DEFAULT dry_run true: only says what restoring would do, column by column, and `blocked`: why it can't be restored now. With dry_run false it first keeps the current setup as a version, then: gone columns come back EMPTY, with their setup; the others get the version's setup, descriptions and order; columns not in the version stay; a column (or an AI column's output column) filled another way now is left, with a note. NOTHING RUNS AND NOTHING IS BILLED, and no cell changes. AI, HTTP API, enrichment and waterfall columns run the restored way next time (control_run rerun mode all bills every row); clean, formula and lookup columns keep their cells until their own tool works them out again (free). Auto-run follows the version, from the rows there now; one paused by hand stays paused. Refused while a run or setup is going on the sheet, or a clean, formula or lookup column is still filling. Needs the write and run scopes (secrets too when a request it puts back reads saved keys); a dry run needs read.

manage_sheet_webhook.description: A sheet's incoming webhook: a secret URL where each JSON event POSTed becomes a new row. get: its state (webhook null when none): on or off, events_received, last_event_at, last_error and its fields. create: adds one (one per sheet) and a column marking the rows it adds. The url is shown until the first event arrives, and only to a key with the write scope; after that it is hidden and rotate makes a new one (the old one stops at once). turn_off: events get 404 and add nothing until turn_on. add_field: json_path (like $.email or $.plan.name) and column, a new column each event fills, as text (default) or as json. remove_field: field_id; its column and values stay. new_token: senders must then send the answer's token (shown once) as Authorization: Bearer <token>, or get 404; an old one stops. remove_token: no token needed. delete: the webhook and its kept events go; its columns and rows stay. manage_table or manage_sheet create with webhook true makes a sheet with one. Every action but get needs the write scope.

list_saved_keys.description: The saved API keys (Settings > External service keys) by name, never their values: for each, created_at and updated_at (UTC), and where it is used: used_in lists each HTTP API, enrichment or waterfall column whose request names the key (sheet_id, sheet_name, table_id, table_name, column, kind, and auto_run when the column fills new rows on its own), and setups the saved setups that name it. At most 20 keys a call, by name, with 10 places and setups each; keys_count, used_in_count and setups_count are whole. For more keys, pass next_after as after; for more of one key's places, pass its name (up to 50 of each). Sheets in the trash and setup versions are left out. Use it to pick a key for a new HTTP request ({{name}} in its URL, headers or body; that needs the secrets scope), or to see what stops working if a key is renamed or deleted. Read-only.

manage_view.description: Create, change or delete a saved view of a sheet: a name, a description, filters (a where) and hidden columns. A view never sorts, changes the column order or touches rows; get_sheet lists the views, and read_rows, export_csv and create_download_link read through one with view. action create makes a copy of the view the app shows (or of from), then sets what you pass: name is required and unique in the sheet, ignoring case; a sheet has at most 50 views. It never switches the view the app shows. change sets only what you pass on view: where and hidden_columns replace what the view had, null clears them (a view with no filters shows every row). delete deletes view (never rows or columns); the Default view can't be deleted, and deleting the view the app shows switches it to Default. Each change is a line in the sheet's History.

transform_column.description: Fill target_column from other columns with a fixed rule, on the server: no AI, no cost. Use it rather than run_ai_column for mechanical text work; for names, company names, emails, domains, phones, Title Case and spaces use clean_column (it keeps cleaning new rows); for a live per-row result use formula_column. Example: turn "8 | B2B SaaS" into a number with regex_extract pattern "^(\\d+)". A call writes at most 10,000 rows or works about 2 seconds, and the rows it wrote stay written. With rows left it answers next_cursor: call again with the same arguments and that cursor. An error after some rows carries next_cursor and rows_done: go on with that cursor, never start over (those rows would get the operation twice). While a pass is unfinished, a call on the same column without its cursor is refused with the cursor; restart:true starts over instead. If the pass's rows move (a sort, an import undone, duplicates removed, rows restored to other places), every call into its column is refused until restart: true, unless it had done no rows. A pass ends at the last row, on restart or when its column is permanently deleted. Returns updated (rows written), created_column and, with rows left, next_cursor. Next: read_rows to check the column.

call_setup.description: Run a saved setup (list_setups) on 1-100 items without a sheet, like a function: each item is an object keyed by the setup's input names, and the answer gives each item's outputs by the columns the setup makes. Use it to enrich a few records for a script or another app; to fill a sheet use apply_setup. COSTS MONEY as apply_setup does: AI steps call your model per item, enrichments spend your treg balance, HTTP API steps send a request per item; clean and formula steps are free. ESTIMATE_ONLY DEFAULTS TO TRUE: the first call prices it and starts nothing; tell the user, then call again with estimate_only:false. max_cost_usd refuses to start when the estimate could pass it (and a step with no known price, unless allow_unpriced). A setup whose requests read saved keys needs the "secrets" scope. Returns a setup_call with its id; poll get_setup_call (wait_seconds) for the results, or pass webhook_id to be told when it finishes. Results are kept 24 hours after it finishes. control_setup_run pauses, resumes or cancels it by that id. get_setup_call.description: Where a setup call (call_setup) is: running, paused, done, failed or cancelled, each step's state and run_id, and once it has finished, results: each item, in the order sent, with its status, error and outputs by column (null when it has no value). With wait_seconds it answers when the call finishes or the time is up, so you poll less. Results are kept 24 hours after the call finishes (keep_until). Read-only.
